children: was in focus on Monday as Citi lowered its price target to $198 from $263, citing “sluggish” checks ahead of the tech company's upcoming third-quarter earnings report.

“Our customer and partner fieldwork continues to suggest sluggish CRM core growth with limited production AI deployments,” Citi analyst Tyler Radke wrote in a note to clients. “We pick up notes of CRM’s ability to more than offset some displacements or license headwinds (consistent with our bus tour takeaways) with other product/pricing expansions, with reseller sales gains consistent in the HSD-LDD range. We continue to expect a slight mechanical reacceleration in organic subscription revenue growth in Q3 and slight [constant currency] beat. We anticipate the outlook on Q4 stays relatively close to implied guide and keep our ex-FX assumptions the same.”
Radke reiterated his Neutral rating on Salesforce.
Delving deeper, Radke said customers are still “cost-conscious” and hesitant to make longer or larger-sized commitments.

“Salesforce appears offsetting the drag through product/price concessions, despite displacements in Marketing and Commerce,” Radke wrote in a note to clients. “We remain cautious, however, with one partner citing meaningful Q4 pipeline degradation from competitive displacements and reduction in contract duration.”

title: Salesforce in focus as Citi lowers price target on 'sluggish' checks ahead of earnings
